config.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Incident postmortem: the checkout outage last Tuesday

personas.name: Ana
personas.goals: A blameless review with real follow-ups
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants budget for a config validation service

personas.name: Ben
personas.goals: Explain what he saw without being blamed
personas.hidden_agenda: Felt alone on the call for the first ten minutes

personas.name: Kofi
personas.goals: Fix the deploy path for payment config

personas.name: Mei
personas.goals: Get customers a clear answer and a goodwill gesture
personas.hidden_agenda: Her team was blindsided by the outage

agenda.title: Root cause and contributing factors
agenda.goal: Understand why the bad config reached production

agenda.title: Customer impact and comms
agenda.goal: Size the impact and decide on customer follow-up

facts.statement: A previous incident with the same cause happened on March 3

beats.summary: Reconstruct the timeline; Ben misremembers the duration
The bad config change, why review missed it, and the repeat incident
Size the impact; Mei overstates the tickets; decide on goodwill credits
Owners for the fixes; one parked question

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, thanks for making time. Let's stay blameless, we're here to fix the system, not find a person.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Appreciated.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Let's start with the timeline. Ben, you were on call, can you walk us through it?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Sure. From what I saw, errors started at twelve past two UTC.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: And the alert didn't go to Ben first, it went to the old payments rotation.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, so when did you actually get paged?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: The page fired at fourteen twenty-one. So about nine minutes after it started.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Support saw it before that, for what it's worth. The chat queue spiked almost immediately.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: That's useful. Did support have a way to tell engineering?

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Not really. We posted in the incidents channel but nobody was watching it yet.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, noting that as a gap.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Sorry, someone's at my door, one second.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Once I was on, the error rate was obviously way up. Dashboards were all red.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: In fairness, the dashboard was red for both regions, so it wasn't a single bad host.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: And how long was checkout down overall?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: About half an hour, start to finish.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: I have forty-seven minutes in the incident doc.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Oh, right, I was counting from when I joined, not from the start.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: That's fair, it felt shorter from inside the call.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: When did we decide to roll back?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Once Kofi joined. He spotted the config change pretty fast.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: The short version is, the change was the only deploy in that window, so it was the obvious suspect.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: And the rollback itself was quick?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Six minutes once we started it.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: From the customer side, it was a bit longer, because carts had to be retried.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay. So, the timeline is roughly agreed, with the paging gap as the first thing to dig into.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Yeah, that's accurate.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Root cause. Kofi, what was in the change?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: CHG-4471. It updated the payment provider timeout from milliseconds to seconds, but the value wasn't converted.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: So it was set to five thousand seconds instead of five seconds?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Effectively, yes. Every checkout call waited until the gateway gave up.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: How did that get through review?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: In fairness, the diff looked tiny. One line. The reviewer approved it in a couple of minutes.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Is there any validation on those config values at all?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Type checks, yes. Range checks, no.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: And this isn't the first time, right? We had something similar before.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Yeah, there was the one in February with the retry config, same kind of thing.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: I think that was March third, actually. The retry limit one.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: You're right, March. Early March.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: So we've had the same root cause twice in a few months.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Which is exactly why this matters. Let's stay blameless, but that's a pattern.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Agreed. And in fairness, the fix from March was a wiki page, not a guardrail.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Out of curiosity, did the new office badge readers ever get fixed? Mine still doesn't work.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Mine works on the second floor but not the third.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Facilities said next week, but they've been saying that for a month.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, let's get back to it. Was there a staged rollout for this change?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: No. Payment config goes to all regions at once. That's the deeper problem.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: So two regions went down together instead of one.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Which is why there was nothing healthy to fail over to.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay. Should we require staged rollouts for payment config?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: I think we have to. Maybe one region first with a fifteen-minute bake.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Fifteen minutes would have caught this one easily.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Let's hold that thought for remediation, but I think everyone agrees on the direction.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Someone should really audit the other payment config values too, there might be more unit mismatches.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, customer impact. Mei, what does it look like from your side?

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: From the customer side, it was rough. We had about two thousand tickets in the first day.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: The support dashboard I have says eleven thirty.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Let me check. Oh, yes. Eleven thirty tickets, two thousand was chats plus tickets.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: How many checkouts actually failed?

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Eighteen thousand four hundred attempts. Some of those are the same customers retrying.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Do we know how many unique customers that is?

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: And revenue? Finance asked me yesterday and I didn't have a number.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Estimated revenue at risk is two hundred and twelve thousand.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: At risk, not lost. A lot of those people came back and bought later.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Some did. Some told us they went to a competitor.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: What did the error rate peak at? I want it in the doc.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Around forty percent, I think.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: It was higher than that. Sixty-four at the peak. I have the screenshot.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Sixty-four. Okay, that's worse than I remembered.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: And for the monthly availability target, we're over budget now, right?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Way over. The target's ninety-nine point nine five, and one outage like this blows the month.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Can we do something for affected customers? A credit, a discount code?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Finance will have opinions.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Finance always does. But I think a goodwill code is reasonable here.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Maybe ten percent off the next order?

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: That sounds right to me. Kofi, Ben, any objections?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: None.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: None from me.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay. We're sending a ten percent goodwill code to every customer with a failed checkout. That's agreed.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Thank you. I'll draft the customer email today and send it to Ana for review.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay, remediation. Let's get owners on these.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: First one's mine. I'll add range validation for every payment timeout and retry value, starting this sprint.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Great. And staged rollouts for payment config?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: I think we said yes in principle.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Then let's make it official. Payment config changes go to one region first, with a fifteen-minute bake, starting Monday.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Good. That would have saved us.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Paging. Ben, can you fix the rotation so payment alerts go to the current on-call?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Yes. I'll move the payment alerts to the main on-call rotation by Thursday.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: And support needs a way to escalate. The channel didn't work.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: What would work for your team?

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Honestly, a button in the support tool that pages on-call directly.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: That's probably a quick integration. Maybe we look at it next quarter?

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Let's not commit to a quarter yet. We can pick it up offline.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: That's fair.

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: Should we also add an alert on checkout latency, not just errors?

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Yes, the latency went crazy minutes before the errors did.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: I'll add the latency alert to our SLO dashboard work and own that one.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Someone should probably write up the unit conversion gotcha for the wiki too.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: We have a wiki page already, that's part of the problem.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Fair point.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Do we need an exec summary for this, or is the doc enough?

turns.speaker: Ben
turns.text: I'm just glad we got through it.

turns.speaker: Ana
turns.text: Okay. I think we've got good owners. Thanks everyone, this was a really good review.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.text: Thanks, Ana.

turns.speaker: Kofi
turns.text: Thanks all.
